summary: IonQ announced it will make the first on-premise quantum computing deployment at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC), installing an IonQ Superion 256 system directly linked to an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink, with workloads orchestrated by the open NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform; the partners will research quantum-GPU system design, hybrid software and applications in finance, materials science and drug discovery, with installation scheduled for 2027.
quote: IonQ plans to install a Superion 256 quantum computer at NVIDIA’s Accelerated Quantum Research Center, making it the center’s first on-premise quantum computing deployment. … The system will connect directly to an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 platform through NVQLink and use CUDA-Q to coordinate hybrid quantum-classical workloads. … The partners will research quantum-GPU system design, hybrid software and applications in finance, materials science and drug discovery, with installation scheduled for 2027. … Today, IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) announced that it will be the first on-premise quantum computing deployment at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC). … As part of the partnership, an IonQ Superion 256 system will be installed at the NVAQC and directly linked with an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink , with workloads orchestrated by the open NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform.

summary: NVIDIA reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 (quarter ended 26 July 2026) revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year, of which $89 billion — roughly 92.5% of total revenue — came from the data center segment. Net income was $59.68 billion, up 126%, and earnings per share were $2.46, up 128%. Operating expenses were $8.4 billion for the quarter and gross margin was 75%.
quote: What stands out in Nvidia's most recent earnings report is that the company is still growing at a triple-digit rate. Revenue in the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (ending July 26, 2026) was $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year ago. Of that, $89 billion, or roughly 92.5% of the company's total revenue, came from its data center segment. … Net income was $59.68 billion, up 126% from a year ago, and earnings per share of $2.46 were up 128% from last year. Nvidia is very profitable -- its operating expenses totaled only $8.4 billion for the quarter, and its gross margin was an impressive 75%.

summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang said the company is the only one that creates and builds an entire AI factory platform, and that the part of the market made up of sovereign AI, regional AIs, neoclouds, AI start-ups and enterprises represents about half of NVIDIA's business and is growing 100% a year.
quote: "We're the only company in the world that creates and builds, offers an entire AI factory platform, a full-stack system. And customers can still mix and match," CEO Jensen Huang said. "However, most companies just don't have the skills to do that or desire to do that. And so, there's an entire part of the market that we experience growth. There's sovereign AI, there're regional AIs, there're neoclouds, there're AI start-ups, there're enterprises, where we're seeing -- which represents about half of our business, and that's growing 100% a year."
